children: China's aluminium exports eased in August from a month earlier but remained elevated, with shipments so far this year up nearly 17% as supply disruptions in the Middle East continued to drive overseas demand for Chinese material.
Exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium products fell 2.6% to 626,000 metric tons last month from 643,000 tons in July, customs data showed on Tuesday.

Shipments remained near the elevated levels seen in June, when exports hit a record 695,000 tons, and reached 4.665 million tons in the first eight months of the year, up 16.7% from the nearly 4 million tons recorded in the year-earlier period.
China has stepped up exports of aluminium alloy and semi-manufactured products this year as disruptions to production and shipments from Gulf producers tightened supply elsewhere.
The increase has also been supported by ample supply in China, the world's biggest aluminium producer, where sluggish domestic demand has made overseas markets more attractive for producers.
